title.rendered: Learning to Enter That Rest: Faith Is Ceasing from Our Works | Living from Rest, Day 3

excerpt.rendered: Hebrews 4:11 tells believers to be diligent to enter that rest. The paradox: we strive to stop striving. Day 3 of Living from Rest unpacks the one effort God asks for.

content.rendered:
There is one strain of effort God does ask from a resting believer. It is the effort to stop performing. That effort is called faith.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, November 3, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 3

Today’s Scripture

“Let us therefore be diligent to enter that rest, lest anyone fall according to the same example of disobedience.”
Hebrews 4:11 (NKJV)

“For he who has entered His rest has himself also ceased from his works as God did from His.”
Hebrews 4:10 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Hebrews 4:11 contains one of the great paradoxes of the Christian life. Be diligent, the writer says, to enter rest. Work hard, in other words, at ceasing from your work. Strive to stop striving. At first glance it reads like a contradiction. But every believer who has walked with God for any length of time knows exactly what it means. There is a kind of effort required to live from rest. It is just not the effort you were taught to put in.

Hebrews 4:11, in the NKJV, says, “Let us therefore be diligent to enter that rest.” The AMPC says, “Let us therefore be zealous and exert ourselves and strive diligently to enter that rest [of God, to know and experience it for ourselves].” The TPT says, “So then we must give our all and be eager to experience this faith-rest life, so that no one falls short.”

What are we being zealous for? Verse 10 tells us: ceasing from our own works. Not ceasing from the work God has given us. Ceasing from the works we were doing to earn Him. The believer still gets up in the morning and goes to the office, the farm, the clinic, the pulpit, the kitchen, the keyboard. Rest is not laziness. Rest is working from a place where you are no longer trying to purchase God’s favour by what you produce.

So the diligence of Hebrews 4 is a diligence of faith. We take pains to believe. We refuse to let the striving spirit creep back in. We confront the thought that whispers, “If you do not do more, God will not love you as much.” We silence the thought that says, “Your rest is suspicious; good Christians stay anxious.” We lay down the religious treadmill and we stand on what Jesus finished.

If you have been trying to earn an acceptance you already have, today is the day to stop. Jesus did not die so that you could spend your Christian life auditioning for His love. He died so that you could rest in it. Enter the rest. Be diligent about it. Fight to believe you are already loved, already accepted, already welcome, already home.

What Diligence to Rest Looks Like

You preach the gospel to yourself. Every day, you remind your own soul what Jesus has already done.

You refuse performance Christianity. You do your work from acceptance, not for acceptance.

You guard your pace. You build margin, Sabbath, prayer and quiet into the week, as a holy habit.

Declaration

I will be diligent to enter His rest. I will fight to believe what Jesus has already won. I cease from the works I was doing to earn God; I take up the works He has given me, and I do them from a settled heart. I am loved, accepted, and welcome in Christ. I will not audition today for a love I already have. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
